proof: Let v=sum_i B_i p_i for quadratic Bernstein weights B_i>=0 and sum_i B_i=1. Exact zero controls contribute nothing.
For a signed unit X/Y axis n, require n dot p_i>0 for every nonzero full-XYZ control. No common strictly positive signed axis leaves the old zero unchanged.
Compute U_i with two positive additions, each rounded outward using nextafter(+infinity). Thus U_i>=||p_i||_1>=||p_i||_2. Nonfinite/overflow upper bounds fail closed.
Compute l_i=nextafter((n dot p_i)/U_i,0). For finite binary64 arithmetic this is an inward lower bound. Set L=min_i l_i for each valid axis and take the largest valid axis certificate.
With S=sum_i B_i||p_i||_2>=||v||_2, n dot v_XY>=L*S. Therefore ||v_XY||_2/||v||_2>=L whenever v is nonzero.
The certificate is a geometric speed-ratio lower bound. It does not grant heading permission, physical rest, motion authority or source freshness.
guards_unchanged: Fallback is used only when the original final quadraticPlanarScale return is zero; every original positive result, including a real tiny cusp cap, is returned unchanged.

Nonzero vertical controls, true opposing/cusp hulls, all-zero controls, nonfinite inputs and unrepresentable certificate values remain zero unless an actual common signed axis proves a positive ratio.
